payload.stem: Which of the following best describes the postcondition of the method mystery (what is true about the returned value)?

options.text: It returns the number of times the character c appears in s.
options.why: The loop examines every one-character piece of s and increases n whenever the piece equals c, so n counts the appearances.

options.text: It returns the position of the first appearance of c in s, or -1 if c does not appear.
options.why: The method never returns a position; the loop continues after a match and returns the count n.

options.text: It returns the number of characters of s that are different from c.
options.why: The loop increases n when a piece equals c, so it counts the matches rather than the non-matches.

options.text: It returns true if s contains c at least once and false otherwise.
options.why: The return type is int, so the method returns a count, not a boolean.

payload.stem: Which of the following is the weakest precondition (the least restrictive condition) that guarantees the method perItem will not throw an exception?

options.text: total is divisible by count.
options.why: The division of ints never throws an exception when there is a remainder; the remainder is simply dropped.

options.text: total is greater than 0.
options.why: The value of total does not matter; total can be 0 or negative without any exception.

options.text: count is greater than 0.
options.why: This is stronger than needed: a negative count such as -3 also works, so it is not the weakest precondition.

options.text: count is not 0.
options.why: Integer division by 0 throws an ArithmeticException, and every other value of count (including negative ones) works.
